title: International audience growth drives Live Nation to  $7.7 billion Q2 revenue
summary: Live Nation has revealed that international markets drove 10% growth in its global audiences in Q2, as the company reported revenue of $7.7 billion for the quarter, up 9% year-on-year. These numbers brought company-wide operating income to $522 million, a 7% rise, though executives said the timing of major tours and ongoing investment in the company’s expanding venue and festival portfolio meant that the adjusted operating income (AOI) figure showed only 2% growth. title: G! Festival: Inside one of the world’s most remote music festivals
summary: For an archipelago of just 55,000, the Faroe Islands are producing more than their fair share of talent. Teitur, Eivør, Greta Svabo Bech and Joe & the Shitboys are among the best-known exports of the 18 islands, located between Iceland and Norway in the North Atlantic Ocean. Bech collaborated with Deadmau5 on the Grammy-nominated Raise Your Weapon, while the Shitboys have been continuously championed as the “best band in the world” on Iggy Pop’s radio show and at his concerts. title: Live Nation reveals plans for South America’s largest indoor arena in São Paulo
summary: Live Nation has announced plans to develop Brazil’s first purpose-built music venue, the 21,000-capacity São Paulo Arena, which will reportedly become the largest indoor arena for live entertainment in South America. The São Paulo Arena will be located within the Cidade Center Norte district, Brazil’s most comprehensive planned urban living neighbourhood. The venue is being developed through a joint venture with the district, and is poised to create a leading entertainment and cultural hub. title: ‘Different languages’: SE Asia stadium touring hampered by public-private ‘misalignment’
summary: South-East Asian cities are losing out on international stadium tours as promoters fail to frame concerts “in public value terms” for governments, according to a leading events executive in the region. title: Record 233 million tune in to Tomorrowland livestreams
summary: Global viewership for Tomorrowland swelled by over 20% for the Belgian electronic festival’s 2026 edition, raising the bar to a record 233 million views across digital livestreams, demonstrating the value of democratising access for international festival brands.
